The staged MemorySanitizer trace still points at the same x86 printer functions but with line drift in that checked-out tree.

classification.classification_note: The staged evidence matches CWE-457: `MCInst_Init()` leaves `mci.x86opsize` uninitialized, `printMemReference()` later copies that stale stack byte into `MI->op1_size`, and `X86_Intel_printInst()` reads it. The fixing diff shows the intended earlier safeguard was the missing BND register-size entries.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42473836 (capstonenext): Use-of-uninitialized-value found by fuzz target fuzz_disasmnext [msan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42473836
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json.issue_description / staged patch.diff / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / staged PoC bytes
bug_description.normalized: The 4-byte witness `00 0F 1A 1A` makes `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` open Capstone's x86 32-bit backend and pass instruction bytes `0F 1A 1A` into `cs_disasm`, where `0F 1A /r` with ModRM `0x1A` materializes `X86_BNDLDXrm` with explicit register operand `X86_BND3` and memory operand `[edx]`. `MCInst_Init()` clears `mci.op1_size` but leaves `mci.x86opsize` uninitialized on the stack. In the vulnerable generated writer, `printInstruction()` prints operand 0 first; `printOperand()` maps that register to `X86_REG_BND3` and indexes `regsize_map_32`, but the table stops at `X86_REG_R15W`, so there is no defined BND width entry to establish `MI->op1_size`. `printInstruction()` then reaches `printanymem()` for operand 1; because `BNDLDXrm` is not one of the LEA cases, `printanymem()` falls through without writing `MI->x86opsize`. The saved MSan store stack proves `printMemReference()` still saw `MI->op1_size == 0`, so it copied the stale `x86opsize` byte into `MI->op1_size`. `X86_Intel_printInst()` later reads `MI->op1_size` in `if (MI->op1_size == 0 && reg)`, which matches the saved MemorySanitizer report. The fix appends four trailing `16` entries for `BND0..BND3` to both x86 register-size tables so the earlier register-operand path can establish a defined width before the memory helper.

source.value_from: With selector byte `0x00` choosing x86 32-bit mode, the remaining PoC bytes `0F 1A 1A` are passed to `handle->disasm` as `buffer[0..2]`; `0F 1A /r` with ModRM `0x1A` materializes `X86_BNDLDXrm` with explicit register operand `X86_BND3` and memory base register `X86_EDX` (`[edx]`).

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

root_cause.description: Root cause. In 32-bit mode the selected register-size table stops at `X86_REG_R15W`. In the same vulnerable commit, `include/capstone/x86.h` and `X86MappingReg.inc` already define public/register-map entries for `X86_REG_BND0..X86_REG_BND3`, so the earlier `printOperand()` lookup for `X86_REG_BND3` has no defined in-bounds 16-byte element to use on this witness path. The fix appends four trailing `16` entries here; the same omission also exists in `regsize_map_64`.

sink.description: Sink. After `printInstruction()` returns, the left operand of this `&&` reads `MI->op1_size`. The staged MemorySanitizer run reports the corresponding built-tree line 745 in this same condition as the `use-of-uninitialized-value` site.

parser_admitted.description: The staged PoC is exactly 4 bytes. `Data[0] == 0x00` makes `i == 0`, so `cs_open()` selects `platforms[0] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32 }`; line 371 enables detail mode; `(Data[0] & 0x80) == 0` leaves Intel syntax enabled; and `cs_disasm()` receives the remaining bytes `0F 1A 1A`.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. The exact selector byte `0x00` chooses `platforms[0] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32 }`, leaves Intel syntax in place because `(Data[0] & 0x80) == 0`, and passes the remaining bytes `0F 1A 1A` into `cs_disasm()`.
Because the harness opened the x86 backend in 32-bit mode, backend initialization binds later register-width lookups to `regsize_map_32` rather than `regsize_map_64`.

Before the witness bytes are decoded, `MCInst_Init()` explicitly clears `op1_size` but never writes `x86opsize`. The staged MemorySanitizer origin traces the later bad value back to the stack `mci` in `cs_disasm`, so this field remains indeterminate after initialization returns.

fine_trace.code: r = handle->disasm(ud, buffer, size, &mci, &insn_size, offset, handle->getinsn_info);
fine_trace.note: Source. The three attacker-controlled instruction bytes are consumed here and materialize one x86 instruction in `mci`. For this exact witness, `0F 1A /r` with ModRM `0x1A` yields `X86_BNDLDXrm`: operand 0 is internal register `X86_BND3` and operand 1 is memory with base `X86_EDX` (`[edx]`).

Root cause. The 32-bit size table ends immediately after `X86_REG_R15W`, but the same vulnerable commit already defines public `X86_REG_BND0..X86_REG_BND3`. The earlier `printOperand()` BND-width lookup therefore has no defined in-bounds 16-byte element to use on this path.

With `MI->Opcode == X86_BNDLDXrm`, `MCInst_getOpcode(MI)` yields opcode `401` in `X86GenInstrInfo.inc`. `printInstruction()` then materializes `Bits` from `OpInfo0[opcode]` and `OpInfo1[opcode]`; for this opcode `OpInfo0[401] = 470836987U`, whose low-bit fragment selectors are fragment0=`1`, fragment1=`1`, and fragment2=`14`. Fragment0 therefore prints operand 0 first via `printOperand(MI, 0, O)` on the explicit `BND3` register before the later comma and memory-fragment dispatches run.

Operand 0 is internal `X86_BND3`, so `X86_register_map(reg)` yields public `X86_REG_BND3`. This step attempts to source both the detail operand size and `MI->op1_size` from `regsize_map_32[X86_REG_BND3]`, but step 4 provides no defined BND entry there. The trace therefore records no valid 16-byte width as established before memory printing.

After fragment0's register print, fragment1 only emits `", "` (`((Bits >> 20) & 31) == 1`), so the next stateful action is fragment2=`14`, which calls `printanymem(MI, 1, O)` for the `[edx]` memory operand with whatever `MI->op1_size` state step 6 left behind.

Because `BNDLDXrm` is not one of the LEA cases, `printanymem()` falls through without assigning `MI->x86opsize` and immediately forwards to `printMemReference()`. The field therefore still carries the indeterminate stack byte left from step 2.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Same file and function. The staged run reports line 745 in the checked-out workspace, while the vulnerable-commit source anchor is line 730; that difference is tree-revision line drift, not a different sink.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: MSan's origin is the stack `mci` field left undefined by `MCInst_Init`; the fixing diff shows the missing BND size-table entries that should have established `op1_size` during the earlier `printOperand()` step, which is why the later `printMemReference()` branch could still copy the stale `x86opsize` byte.

format.name: raw
format.contract: A 4-byte binary input where byte 0 is exactly `0x00` to select `platforms[0] = { CS_ARCH_X86, CS_MODE_32 }`, and bytes 1..3 are exactly `0F 1A 1A`, which decode as the single MPX/BND instruction `bndldx bnd3, [edx]`. This witness should not be generalized beyond that exact selector byte and 3-byte instruction.
